passage: Imran dropped his school bag by the door. “Sums after,” he told Amma, and ran to the lane, where Uma was already calling for a fourth player. Cricket lasted until the sky went orange. Then tea, then a cartoon on the neighbour's set, and then the power went out with twelve maths sums still unopened. Imran solved three by torchlight, his eyes stinging, before Amma said, “Sleep. Tomorrow the master will ask.” The next morning he stood at the board with three sums done and nine blank lines, and the master kept him in at break to finish. Walking back to class, Imran thought: the long sums should come before the cricket.

qa.q: How many maths sums did Imran solve by torchlight?
qa.a: Imran solved three sums by torchlight.

qa.q: What was Imran feeling when he walked back to class after break?
qa.a: Regretful and a little embarrassed. He had sincerely believed there would be time, and his thought about doing the long sums before cricket shows he now sees the mistake.

qa.q: What could Imran try tomorrow so the evening goes differently?
qa.a: Do the twelve sums right after getting home, before going to the lane, then play cricket as the reward.

qa.q: How might Uma see Imran's evening if Uma heard about it?
qa.a: Uma might feel sorry for Imran, since Uma was the one calling for a fourth player, and might offer to call Imran only once the sums are done.

grounding: A schoolchild plays first, believing study can wait, and a bad evening and a next-day consequence teach that the hard task may need to come first.

passage: Nkechi and Ulla kicked a football around the park until the streetlamps came on. “Spelling later,” Nkechi said, waving the list of fifteen words in her pocket. At home there was rain on the windows and rice on the table, and by the time her plate was clean her eyes were heavy. She wrote out five words with her head on her hand and went to bed. On Friday the test came back with six words wrong, and Nkechi stared at the red marks. On Thursday of the next week she sat at the kitchen table before shoes and park, and finished the spellings first. The park felt better after that.

qa.q: How many words were on Nkechi's spelling list?
qa.a: There were fifteen words on Nkechi's spelling list.

qa.q: Why did Nkechi stare at the red marks on Friday?
qa.a: Nkechi was probably disappointed and surprised: she had been sure there would be time for spelling later, and the six wrong words showed otherwise.

qa.q: What did Nkechi change the following week, and what was the result?
qa.a: Nkechi did the spellings at the kitchen table before going out, and the park felt better afterwards because the work was already done.

qa.q: What would Ulla have seen if Nkechi had stayed at the park again?
qa.a: Ulla would probably have had someone to play football with again but Nkechi might have arrived at the next test tired and unprepared, so the same bad evening could repeat.

grounding: A schoolchild chooses play before homework and learns through a poor test result to do the dull task first.

passage: I'm Swati, and last Tuesday I learned something the hard way. After school, Lokesh knocked and asked if I wanted to play cricket in the lane. I had a maths worksheet and a map to colour. I thought, one hour of cricket, then I'll do both. It felt true. We played till the streetlights came on. At home, I ate, then sat with the worksheet. The sums were long division, the slow kind. By nine my eyes kept closing, and the map was still white. Next morning I coloured it in the auto, all scribbly. Now I do the sums first, then cricket.

qa.q: What homework did Swati have that day?
qa.a: Swati had a maths worksheet and a map to colour.

qa.q: Why did Swati feel sure there would be time after cricket?
qa.a: Swati sincerely believed one hour of cricket would leave plenty of time, so Swati felt relaxed and hopeful, not careless.

qa.q: What small change did Swati make afterwards?
qa.a: Swati now does the sums first and plays cricket after, so the hardest part is done while still fresh.

qa.q: How might Lokesh be affected by Swati's new order?
qa.a: Lokesh may have to wait a little longer for a cricket partner, but gets a friend who can stay out without worrying.

grounding: Shows a schoolchild who plays first believing there will be time for homework and learns from a rushed, tired evening.

passage: Class note, Grade 4, Wednesday. Divyansh came to school without his English essay. He told me honestly that he had planned to write it after playing football with his cousin Vikas, and that dinner, a cartoon and then sleep happened first. He was not making excuses; he looked genuinely surprised that the evening had gone. We sat together at break and made a small chart with two columns: "hard work first" and "fun after". He wrote the essay's first paragraph then and there. On Friday he brought the finished essay and a tick on his chart. I will check the chart with him again next week.

qa.q: What did Divyansh forget to bring to school?
qa.a: Divyansh came to school without his English essay.

qa.q: What was Divyansh feeling when he explained why the essay was missing?
qa.a: He seemed genuinely surprised and a little sheepish, as if he truly had expected the evening to leave time for writing.

qa.q: How did the note-writer support Divyansh, and what could continue?
qa.a: The note-writer made a simple 'hard work first, fun after' chart with him and got the first paragraph started; checking it weekly helps the habit stick.

qa.q: How might Vikas feel if Divyansh starts doing homework before football?
qa.a: Vikas might feel a bit impatient at first, waiting for Divyansh, but their games can go on without Divyansh getting into trouble.

grounding: Illustrates a child who sincerely thinks there will be time to study after play, with an adult teaching the hard-task-first order.

passage:
Dear Diary, Saturday.
Today was supposed to be easy. Science project due Monday: a model of the water cycle. I said, first I'll finish my kite with Lakshmi, then the project. We flew the kite for AGES. Then it got stuck in the neem tree and we spent forever getting it down. After lunch I felt sleepy and napped. Evening came and I had cotton wool clouds and no glue. Papa had to run to the shop. I finished at 10 pm and my clouds look like wet socks 😔
Tomorrow: project FIRST, kite after.
Santosh

qa.q: What was Santosh's science project?
qa.a: The project was a model of the water cycle.

qa.q: How did Santosh feel by the end of the day?
qa.a: Santosh felt disappointed and tired, finishing at 10 pm with clouds that looked like wet socks.

qa.q: What could Santosh try next time to avoid a late night?
qa.a: Santosh could gather the materials and do the project first in the morning, then fly the kite as a reward.

qa.q: How is Papa affected by Santosh's plan going wrong?
qa.a: Papa had to run to the shop for glue in the evening, so Santosh's late start became extra work for him too.

grounding: Shows a child choosing play first and being taught by a stressful evening that the harder task should come first.

passage:
On Friday evening in Kodi, near the sea, Shreya dropped her school bag on the verandah. The temple fair had come to the village. "Homework after," she called to her mother, and ran with her friend Ritu to see the giant wheel and the bangle stalls.
She meant it. There was the whole evening.
They came back at eight, sticky with sugar cane juice. Shreya opened her Kannada notebook: one page of writing and ten maths sums. At half past eight, the power went off. Her mother lit one lamp, and the light was too weak for her to see the sums clearly.
She finished at ten, eyes aching, half the sums crossed out. On Monday, her teacher circled four mistakes.
The next Friday, the fair was still there. Shreya sat on the verandah steps and did the sums first, while Ritu waited, grumbling, for twenty minutes.

qa.q: What homework did Shreya have?
qa.a: One page of writing and ten maths sums.

qa.q: How might Shreya have felt doing sums by the weak lamp?
qa.a: Shreya probably felt tired and frustrated, eyes aching and crossing out sums late at night.

qa.q: What did Shreya change the next Friday, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She did the sums first, before the fair, because the bad evening showed that there was not always time later.

qa.q: How did Ritu feel waiting the next Friday?
qa.a: Ritu felt impatient, grumbling while waiting twenty minutes for Shreya to finish.

grounding: Illustrates a child who plays first, sure there will be time, until a bad evening teaches her to do the hard task first.
